title: Samples playground gatekeeping notes
body:
Context:
Quick weekly checkpoint from the Samples Playground sync (feb 17). Mostly focused on gating rules for what can land in the public examples repo and how the interactive playground should curate / surface those examples. This is a working note; lots of open questions at the bottom.

Attendees (quick): Priya (owner), Liam, Aisha, Marcus, Dana, + 2 UX folks joined for the last 15m.

What triggered this meeting:
- Growing noise in samples repo: 18 new example PRs last week, several with hard-coded API keys and bad-quality prompts.
- Playground showing broken snippets because some samples depend on unreleased SDK helpers.
- Onboarding feedback: new hires and external folks report friction finding a small, reproducible quickstart for local dev.

Observed problems (concrete):
- Fragmented templates: we have 5 different quickstart templates (node, python, docker, cloud-run, bare-http). Each one has slightly different env var names and different setup steps. Confusion -> onboarding friction.
- CI flakiness: samples-runner job failing nondeterministically on macOS matrix. 6 flakes last 2 weeks, root cause appears to be cache invalidation in the sample-build step. Ticketed as JIRA-DEVEXP-1278.
- Secrets leaks: 2 PRs contained example API keys; reviewers flagged but they briefly landed in master and caused ephemeral spikes in usage. Need safer pre-merge hooks.
- Playground curation: playground auto-imports any example labeled `playground-ready` but maintainers haven't been consistent with that label. UX shows outdated screenshots when examples change.

Decisions made (quick):
- Gate rule v0.1: samples must pass 'samples-smoke' job and include a short metadata file (SAMPLE.md) with fields: description, required-sdk-version, public? (y/n), playground-ready (y/n). If playground-ready = y, must include a deterministic run script.
- Reject examples with hard-coded credentials or long-form conversational prompts that rely on private context. Examples should be deterministic and runnable locally w/ a single env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- CI safeguard: add a pre-merge check to detect tokens-looking-like-strings and fail fast. Liam to prototype a small grep-and-fuzzy-checker.
- Playground sync cadence: playground team will do a weekly sweep (Friday morning) to check newly labeled playground-ready examples before they appear in UI.

Proposals (next actions / spikes):
- Template consolidation spike (2 sprint days): propose canonical quickstart templates for Node+Python+Docker. Goal: align env var names and top-of-file comments. Owner: Aisha. Deliverable: PR with consolidated templates + migration guide.
- Samples linter: implement rule set for sample quality (no secrets, no >10s external calls, clear README, testable). Marcus will draft initial rules and add to samples-runner.
- Playground deterministic runner: create a lightweight runner that runs examples in a sandbox mode and captures stdout/stderr + snapshot screenshots (for UI). Needs to be container-friendly. Dana + UX to scope.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Aisha: create consolidated quickstart PR draft + checklist (ETA: 2026-02-28).
- Liam: prototype token-check pre-merge hook + add to samples-runner (branch: ci/token-guard) (ETA: 2026-02-20).
- Marcus: write samples linter rules doc + initial rule set in repo (ETA: 2026-02-24).
- Dana: define minimal playground contract (input artifacts, screenshot resolution, run timeout) and sync with UX (ETA: 2026-02-22).
- Priya: coordinate weekly playground sweep rota and publish in README (ETA: 2026-02-18).

Risks & Notes:
- We must be careful not to gate early-stage community contributions too strictly; maintainers recommended an "auto-sandbox" label path for community samples that are flagged but not surfaced until maintainer approval.
- Consolidating templates will create churn for existing sample authors; propose a migration automated script (rename env var mapping) to reduce churn.
- The token-checker must avoid false positives for code that happens to have long hex strings (e.g., model IDs). Need allowlist patterns.

Unresolved questions / open threads:
- How strict should the deterministic-run requirement be? Do we accept short-lived external API calls (e.g., weather API) for demo purposes? (open)
- Should we expose a curated subset of playground examples to public vs internal? implications for analytics and support.
- Who is the final arbiter for playground removal when examples break? (suggestion: rotating "playground steward" weekly)

Quick notes from UX segment (last 15m):
- UX wants small, screenshot-friendly examples that complete within 6s and produce concise text outputs.
- Prefer fixtures over network calls for screenshots to avoid flakiness in CI.
- Screenshot naming convention: repo/path--example-name--sha.png (to make diffs easier).

Follow-ups to capture in Confluence:
- Move the gate rules to CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-453 -> "Samples Gatekeeping & Playground Contract" and link from README.
- Add migration notes and a short how-to for contributors in samples/CONTRIBUTING.md.

Quick wins to ship this week:
- Add token-check pre-merge hook (Liam).
- Publish weekly sweep rota (Priya).
- Short README snippet for maintainers about labeling (playground-ready vs community-sandbox) (Dana).

Notes-to-self style: "If people keep abusing main with messy demos, the playground UX will degrade quickly and we'll get support tickets. Better to define minimal friction gating now than fight cleanup later."

Raw links / refs captured during the call:
- github: github.com/redwood/samples/pulls (we looked at 10 active PRs)
- jira: JIRA-DEVEXP-1278 (ci flakes)
- confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-453
- slack thread: #devexp "playground drift" (ts:1676567200)

Meeting end. Next sync: quick status check in 1 week (standup channel update + brief Friday async note).
